title: Analytical Chemistry
description: An analytical chemistry course covering measurement science, data quality and metrology, statistics and calibration, sampling and sample preparation, chemical equilibria, titrations, gravimetry, electroanalysis, molecular and atomic spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, method validation, chemometrics, and quality assurance.

topics.title: Analytical Chemistry as Measurement Science
topics.description: Define analytical chemistry as the science of asking chemical questions, designing measurements, and defending results.

children.title: Analytical questions and decision context
children.description: Students learn that an analytical method starts with a decision, not with an instrument.

children.title: Analyte, matrix, and interferents
children.description: This subtopic builds vocabulary for what is measured, what surrounds it, and what can distort the result.

children.title: Analytical workflow
children.description: The goal is to see analysis as a chain of choices from sampling to reporting.

topics.title: Data Quality, Significant Figures, and Chemical Metrology
topics.description: Build the habits needed to report measurements with appropriate precision, traceability, and uncertainty.

children.title: Measurement units and traceability
children.description: Students connect chemical measurements to standards so results can be compared across labs.

children.title: Significant figures and reporting
children.description: This subtopic prevents false precision and teaches defensible result formatting.

children.title: Precision, accuracy, and bias
children.description: Students separate repeatability from truthfulness and learn how systematic error enters.

topics.title: Statistics, Error, Calibration, and Detection Limits
topics.description: Use statistical tools to decide whether analytical data are reliable, different, linear, and fit for purpose.

children.title: Descriptive statistics
children.description: Students summarize repeated measurements and estimate the spread of analytical data.

children.title: Inference and outliers
children.description: This subtopic gives tools for deciding whether results differ meaningfully.

children.title: Calibration and detection
children.description: Students learn how instrument response becomes concentration and where the useful measurement range begins.

topics.title: Sampling, Sample Preparation, and Method Workflow
topics.description: Understand that the measurement is only as good as the sample, preparation, and chain of handling.

children.title: Sampling design
children.description: Students learn why sampling error often dominates instrument error.

children.title: Sample handling and preservation
children.description: This subtopic protects analytes from loss, contamination, or chemical change.

children.title: Preparation techniques
children.description: Students compare preparation methods that isolate analytes and reduce matrix effects.

topics.title: Chemical Equilibria for Analysis
topics.description: Use equilibrium chemistry as the quantitative engine behind titrations, separations, and speciation.

children.title: Equilibrium constants and mass balance
children.description: Students use equilibrium expressions to predict analytical reactions and species distributions.

children.title: Speciation calculations
children.description: This subtopic explains how analytes distribute among chemical forms.

children.title: Equilibrium in method design
children.description: Students learn to choose conditions that make measurements selective and complete.

topics.title: Acid-Base Titrations and pH Measurements
topics.description: Master acid-base analysis, buffers, titration curves, indicators, and glass-electrode pH measurement.

children.title: Acid-base theory and buffers
children.description: Students use proton-transfer equilibria to control and measure solution chemistry.

children.title: Titration curves and endpoints
children.description: This subtopic develops calculation and interpretation of acid-base titrations.

children.title: pH electrodes and measurement
children.description: Students learn how pH is measured and what makes pH readings fail.

topics.title: Complexation and Chelometric Analysis
topics.description: Apply metal-ligand equilibria to selective metal analysis, masking, and EDTA titration design.

children.title: Metal-ligand equilibria
children.description: Students learn how ligands bind metals and how pH affects complex stability.

children.title: EDTA titrations
children.description: This subtopic teaches a central analytical method for metal-ion determination.

children.title: Selectivity control
children.description: Students learn how to make complexometric methods specific enough for real samples.

topics.title: Precipitation, Gravimetry, and Solubility Analysis
topics.description: Use low-solubility reactions for quantitative separations and mass-based determinations.

children.title: Solubility equilibria
children.description: Students use Ksp to predict when precipitates form and dissolve.

children.title: Gravimetric analysis
children.description: This subtopic shows how mass can become a high-accuracy chemical measurement.

children.title: Precipitation titrations
children.description: Students learn endpoint detection in reactions that form insoluble salts.

topics.title: Redox Chemistry and Electroanalytical Methods
topics.description: Analyze electron-transfer reactions and electrochemical signals for concentration and mechanism information.

children.title: Redox equilibria
children.description: Students connect electron transfer to measurable potentials and titration behavior.

children.title: Redox titrations
children.description: This subtopic covers concentration analysis using electron-transfer stoichiometry.

children.title: Electroanalytical techniques
children.description: Students learn how current, potential, and charge report concentration and mechanism.

topics.title: Spectrophotometry and Molecular Spectroscopy
topics.description: Use light absorption and emission to quantify analytes and interpret molecular information.

children.title: Light absorption and Beer-Lambert law
children.description: Students learn the quantitative link between absorbance and concentration.

children.title: UV-Vis and fluorescence methods
children.description: This subtopic develops common molecular methods for sensitive quantitative analysis.

children.title: IR, Raman, and molecular identification
children.description: Students use vibrational spectroscopy to identify functional groups and molecular environments.

topics.title: Atomic Spectroscopy and Elemental Analysis
topics.description: Measure elements with flame, graphite furnace, plasma, and X-ray based techniques.

children.title: Atomic absorption and emission
children.description: Students learn how atomic transitions quantify elements.

children.title: Plasma-based methods
children.description: This subtopic introduces high-performance elemental analysis for trace metals.

children.title: X-ray and surface elemental methods
children.description: Students see complementary approaches for solids, surfaces, and materials.

topics.title: Chromatography and Separation Science
topics.description: Separate complex mixtures and quantify components using GC, HPLC, and modern separation metrics.

children.title: Separation fundamentals
children.description: Students learn the physical metrics that describe chromatographic performance.

children.title: Gas chromatography
children.description: This subtopic covers volatile and semi-volatile analyte separation.

children.title: Liquid chromatography
children.description: Students learn modern LC methods for polar, nonvolatile, and thermally fragile analytes.

topics.title: Mass Spectrometry and Hyphenated Methods
topics.description: Connect ionization, mass analysis, fragmentation, and coupled separations to identification and quantitation.

children.title: Ionization and mass analyzers
children.description: Students learn how molecules become ions and how mass-to-charge is measured.

children.title: Fragmentation and identification
children.description: This subtopic teaches interpretation of mass spectra and molecular evidence.

children.title: Coupled techniques
children.description: Students see how separations and MS combine for complex mixtures.

topics.title: Instrument Signals, Noise, Automation, and Method Validation
topics.description: Understand how instruments convert chemistry into data and how methods are validated for real decisions.

children.title: Signals, noise, and electronics
children.description: Students learn what limits instrumental measurements and how signal quality is improved.

children.title: Automation and lab workflow
children.description: This subtopic connects instruments to modern sample throughput and data handling.

children.title: Method validation
children.description: Students learn the formal criteria for proving an analytical method works.

topics.title: Chemometrics, Multivariate Data, and Analytical Informatics
topics.description: Use modern data tools for calibration, classification, pattern recognition, and high-dimensional chemical data.

children.title: Multivariate calibration
children.description: Students learn how multiple signals can predict concentration when single-wavelength calibration is not enough.

children.title: Pattern recognition and classification
children.description: This subtopic shows how analytical data can identify sample type, source, or authenticity.

children.title: Data integrity and reproducibility
children.description: Students learn modern expectations for trustworthy analytical data.

topics.title: Quality Assurance, Ethics, Safety, and Applied Analytical Projects
topics.description: Integrate QA/QC, lab safety, documentation, ethics, and project design in realistic analytical work.

children.title: Quality control systems
children.description: Students learn the checks that keep routine analytical results reliable over time.

children.title: Ethics, safety, and regulation
children.description: This subtopic frames analytical chemistry as professional work with consequences.

children.title: Applied project design
children.description: Students synthesize the course by designing, validating, and communicating a complete method.
